feature: Ask makes the change straight away, one row per change
summary: Ask now makes the change as soon as the model on this Mac is done: no plan to read, no Run Plan. Each request leaves one row in the Agent group saying what changed, with a switch to turn it off and on and a delete.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Needs Ollama with qwen3:30b (the default). Walks: ask-annotates-a-screenshot-walk, ask-adds-a-title-page-walk, ask-makes-a-pricing-section-walk.

try.do: Open a settings screenshot, press Ask in the title bar, type "annotate the ux with measurements around the major ui elements" and press Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Flip the row's switch off: the measurements go and the screenshot is as it was.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Flip it back on: they come back exactly where they were.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z: the whole request goes and its row reads off. Shift Command Z puts it back.
Open the sample recording, ask "add a title page that says Case 1 before this clip", then flip its row off and on.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: On a blank canvas ask "Make a pricing section on brand", then press the row's trash button: the change goes and so does the row. Command Z brings both back.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click a row's words: what that change made is picked on the canvas, so you can keep going by hand. Right-click the row for Turn Off (or Turn On) and Delete.

evaluate: Does the row's sentence tell you what the request did without reading anything else?
Is a switch plus a trash button the right pair, or would you rather delete live only in the right-click menu?
When a later edit built on a change, the switch refuses and the row says "A later change builds on this." Is that clear enough, or should it offer to take both out?
Rows last for the window's session and are not saved with the file. Is that what you expect?
rough: This goes against the mock's Plan list and Run plan button (agent-generate-wt.html, the Agent group): the user's own words on 2026-10-20 replaced them, recorded in this task (ask-makes-the-change-straight-away-and-each-chan). The row keeps the mock's Last change idea.
Matches the mock's Last change click: clicking a row's words picks what it made on the canvas (the layers it added, or the ones it edited).
A later hand edit to something the agent made (moving a drawn measurement, say) also counts as building on it, so that change can no longer be switched off; it can still be taken back with Command Z.
What the model builds is unchanged by this task: the pricing section still lands as loose text over a card rather than a tidy section.
Every picture shows the window behind another app, so the switch shows grey instead of the accent colour.
